method_note: METHOD NOTE: WebFetch and curl were blocked; every quote below was captured from Google-style search snippets of the cited page (the harness's WebSearch summaries). Quotes are reproduced exactly as the snippet rendered them; where the snippet paraphrased, the fact is marked as a paraphrase in 'quote'. Dates of the form ~YYYY-MM-DD are back-computed from 'N days ago' as of 2026-10-05.

facts.claim: Premise of Fair Value / Fair Pricing Theory as codified by FX Replay
facts.quote: JJ Simon's Fair Value Theory is built on a straightforward market premise: when no new information is available for the market to price in, price is likely to revert toward a reference point known as "fair value."
facts.source_title: JJ Simon's Fair Value Theory Strategy (FX Replay)

facts.claim: Premise as worded in the FX Replay PDF
facts.quote: Fair Value Theory states that if there is no 'new' information for the market to price in, it is most likely going to revert back to 'fair value.' JJ has found 9:30 market open price and 2pm NY afternoon to often act as fair value.
facts.source_title: JJ Simon's Fair Value Theory NQ Strategy Backtesting Reimagined (PDF)

facts.claim: Two fair-value anchors for NQ: 9:30 ET open price and 2:00 PM ET price
facts.quote: For the NQ, Nasdaq-100 futures, JJ has identified two price levels that consistently act as fair value: the 9:30 AM market open price and the 2:00 PM NY afternoon price.
facts.source_title: JJ Simon's Fair Value Theory Strategy (FX Replay)

facts.claim: JJ's own definition: fair price is the market open 95% of the time (implying ~5% of cases use something else; the snippet did not say what)
facts.quote: the fair price is 95% of the time going to be the market open
facts.source_title: The Strategy Behind My $1.6M in Prop Firm Payouts — Transcript (sozai.app)

facts.claim: Summary of JJ's core principle (sozai summary of his video)

facts.claim: FX Replay entry trigger: MSB/BOS plus displacement; fixed 1.5R; no management
facts.quote: All entries require the same two-condition trigger: a Market Structure Break, MSB, or Break of Structure, BOS, confirmed by a strong displacement candle. Once entered, trades target a fixed 1.5R with no active trade management.

facts.claim: FX Replay BOS vs MSB definitions
facts.quote: A BOS, Break of Structure, signals trend continuation, while an MSB, Market Structure Break, signals a potential trend reversal.

facts.claim: FX Replay PDF mechanical MSB definition

facts.claim: FX Replay displacement candle definition (qualitative)
facts.quote: A displacement candle is a candle that closes decisively (with a small 'counter-wick') and ideally is larger than the candles before it.

contradictions: Continuation phase length: JJ says first 5 minutes (sozai $1.6M transcript); FX Replay, AndrewFXTD and youtubesummary say first 10-15 minutes.
Reversion phase: JJ says the remaining 85 minutes to 11:00; FX Replay's filtered test says only the first ~30 minutes after the open and that later reversions have lower probability.
Session start: JJ trades from the open (continuation in the first 5 minutes); FX Replay suggests skipping the first 3 minutes after 09:30.

Fair price definition: JJ says 'the market open' (95% of cases) and 'the 9:30 a.m. open'; FX Replay says 'the 9:30 AM market open price'; the 365-day backtester uses 'the candle right before the NASDAQ opens' (pre-open candle); krisskross18 uses the 9:29 candle OPEN; joetroyer offers six selectable sources (candle before volume spike, session open, 9:29 line, VWAP, prev-day close, manual). No JJ quote was captured specifying the 9:29 close vs the 09:30 print, nor what the 'other 5%' are.

Premium/discount band: joetroyer requires price to reach a +/-38-point band before a reversion signal; no JJ statement of any minimum distance or band was found; FX Replay and AndrewFXTD state no band.

Continuation vs reversion emphasis: JJ says most trades are reversion (85 of 90 minutes) yet also states the simplest continuation model beat the simplest mean-reversion model over 5 years; FX Replay's backtest likewise found continuations had the higher win rate and profit factor.
Trades per day: sozai summary of JJ's video says ~10 trades/day; the Chart Fanatics title says 30 times/day.
Account count: JJ mentions 40 accounts ($100k/month video); Chart Fanatics description says 45+ accounts.
Point value: youtubesummary states one point = $1 on NQ; FX Replay correctly states one NQ point = $20.

Independent results diverge: 365-day backtester PF 1.94 raw / 1.7 optimized (initial ~1.2); FX Replay PF 1.76 overall, ~1.46 for reversion subset; faketrades.in community rates the strategy 1.0 star with 1 'bust'; the 52-trade test was run on EURUSD, which a commenter says misapplies NQ point-based stops.

Payout figure attached to the strategy varies by source and date: $1.2M (youtubesummary, ~Apr 2026), $1.3M (365-day backtester, faketrades), $1.5M (jjwebinar), $1.6M (JJ video), $2M (Chart Fanatics, schedule-call page).
